title: JPMorgan says cyberattack on third-party vendors may have exposed some customer data
date_note: Published November 19; date of the vendor attack not stated.
summary: JPMorgan said in a November 19 post that third parties providing services to the firm were attacked and it believes attackers accessed marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. It says services were not disrupted and it will offer affected customers complimentary credit monitoring where appropriate. Newsweek reports a group called nOn published around 16,000 customer email addresses.
plain: JPMorgan says outside companies it uses were hacked, and some customers' names and email addresses may have been exposed.
exec: Vendor-held customer contact data is a phishing risk and shows how third-party suppliers extend a bank's exposure.
action: JPMorgan customers: be wary of unexpected emails that mention your account; the bank says it will contact affected customers directly where appropriate.
impact: Some customer names and email addresses may be exposed; Newsweek reports nOn published around 16,000 customer email addresses.

validation.note: Newsweek (quotes a JPMorgan spokesman) and Crypto Briefing report independently; vendors not named; leak figure is Newsweek's account of nOn's post.

review.note: Compared with Newsweek, Crypto Briefing, ABC13, GBHackers: removed unsupported 'bank says no financial data was involved' from action, removed placeholder occurred_at, 16,000 now 'around' per Newsweek (only Newsweek states it), nOn named as Newsweek's account.
